event: Wren wakes on Day 21 to an unknown voice coming from the north through the tree line.
The voice narrates fast to the trail, calling it a disagreement between two hills.
Hadley sits by the cold fire, looking expectant. 'That would be Brecca.'
Brecca comes through the tree line like weather: short, broad, rucksack on one shoulder.
She stops at the clearing's edge, looks at Wren, Hadley and the camp, and says 'Five what?'
Wren stands barefoot in her sleeping clothes before the girl who walked three days to ask.
'Bonds. I have five bonds with places in the Thornwild. I wanted you to know I was real.'
Brecca stares three seconds: 'That tells me nothing.' She is right.
Within ten minutes she drops her pack by Hadley's lean-to and drinks from his skin unasked.
She strides south to the ruins to assess them; Wren follows.
At the hall's east face she lays her hand flat on the wall, reading load, not resonance.
Clay binding between the courses flexes where mortar would crack; that is why it held.
She runs her hands along joints and foundation, each touch a specific assessment.
The hall's lintel has shifted east; she asks if it moved. Wren does not know.
Brecca asks what bonding means: she touched the walls and the System said something?
Wren explains nine days with the threshold stone, nine discoveries, the bond between them.
The language of bonds and depths lands wrong; to Brecca it is a kind of exclusion.
'Nine days. Sitting.' Brecca says she would have lost her mind, and means it.
Theron is already working at the drainage channel when Brecca approaches.
Without looking up he hands her a flat stone: clear the east section, toward the junction.
Brecca crouches beside him and clears silt, given the first useful thing in three days.
They work four silent minutes, which Wren suspects is a record for Brecca.
Brecca reads the six-degree gradient: someone tested this with water before setting stones.
Theron says they tested it with snowmelt and let the first thaw choose the line.
'That is good engineering,' Brecca says, quiet, almost reverent.
Theron shows her a well-built thing and lets her recognize it, explaining nothing.
Brecca's shoulders drop after ten minutes; Theron slows his pace to give her room.
Wren watches and catalogues, but does not join; clearing silt is not her language.
At midday Wren sits with her back to the threshold stone, its vibration in her sternum.
She realizes she answered Brecca with mechanics: she sent her another stat screen.
She thinks the true answer: the stone knows her, and five means the world got bigger five times.
She has not said it. She sits without surveying and lets the afternoon be still.
Back at camp she finds Brecca has framed the seed storage's partial roof into a shelter.
Branch supports in the foundation gaps, floor cleared, bedroll inside, frame tested by weight.
'Good enough.' Built in two hours: 'The roof was already there. I just gave it legs.'
Wren sees new wood against old stone, and says 'Come see the other one.'
In the healer's house next door the [Kept] bond hums; Brecca stops and says 'This is different.'
Wren reads the healer for her: dawn window, worn mortar-bowl, the threshold's daily wear.
Brecca stands in the healer's light and realizes she sleeps next door to it.
'Is that okay? With the bond thing?' 'The bond does not mind.'
Brecca, loud again, wants clay: the seed storage roof shows daylight on the west join.
At the fire Brecca sets a fourth sitting stone, a level slab from the hall's collapse.
Hadley cooks a stew from his Millhaven supplies: the camp's first complex food smell.
Brecca eats fast: 'You cook like someone who pays attention to temperature.'
'I pay attention to most things. It is the family disease.' Brecca laughs, too loud.
She tells the trail as a story: the mirewillow roots, the chair rock, the confident bird.
'You followed a bird,' Theron says. 'The bird was very confident.'
Hadley draws her out about Thorngate, Aldric's inn, and her two weeks of waiting.
Brecca floods: potter parents, a kind innkeeper, and a System that has never spoken.
Wren hears the fear beneath: that the System's silence is a verdict on her.
Theron says the hall's east wall needs repointing, clay lies south: 'I do not know how. You do.'
'Yeah. I do,' Brecca says, quiet, her competence treated as real.
She asks Theron if any of the fourteen families were builders.
'My grandmother's mother was a mason. She dressed the threshold stone.'
Brecca sits six silent seconds, then asks to see the stone in the morning.
'Wren will show you,' Theron says. 'It is her stone.'
After her night sitting at the stone, Wren finds Brecca alone on the healer's threshold.
Wren almost walks past, filing the observation; she sits down beside Brecca instead.
They sit in silence; Wren does not survey or catalogue.
Brecca says she sought a Wayfinder to learn why the System has given her no class at fifteen.
'You walked three days alone to get here,' Wren says. 'You came anyway.'
'That is not nothing.' Wren speaks to the person, with no stats in it.
Brecca's breath catches short of crying; she wipes her dry face and goes to sleep.
Wren hears the frame creak once and hold; she said one true thing, and it is a start.
Wren wakes on Day 22 to Brecca at the hall's east wall at dawn, repointing with clay.
Brecca found the clay deposit, mixed it, and presses it into joints, testing each by hand.
She starts the work before anyone wakes, as Theron did on Day 19; the work is the commitment.
Wren sees Brecca's whole hand reading the wall: that is a form of surveying. She does not say it.
At the threshold stone she feels the thirty-second dawn vibration, restored and steady.
She journals 'Day 22. Four.' and that Brecca, classless, is paying attention.
She writes: people are a harder survey, but might be more important.
Wren, Level 5 with five bonds, is learning to see something she never surveyed; the count climbs.
